summary: Maintains a first-in-first-out table for appended rows, automatically dropping the oldest rows once the configured maximum is reached.

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Callback DAT called for each newly appended row

key_params.name: executeloc
key_params.note: Choose the execution context for row-added callback scripts

key_params.name: fromop
key_params.note: Operator path used when Execute from is set to Specified Operator

key_params.name: clamp
key_params.note: Limit row count to Max Lines

key_params.name: maxlines
key_params.note: Maximum number of rows preserved when clamping

key_params.name: firstrow
key_params.note: Preserve the first row as a header while FIFO rows roll underneath

key_params.name: extension
key_params.note: Edit/view file extension exposed to external editors

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when Extension is set to Custom Extension

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Common DAT node-display word wrap setting

common_gotchas: Rows are normally added by script with appendRow(); placing a DAT upstream is not the primary input pattern.
The default clamp is small enough for logs but may truncate long-running captures unless Max Lines is raised.
Callbacks fire once for each added row, so batch append operations can call user code many times.
Preserving the first row is useful for headers but changes which row is dropped when capacity is reached.
key_concepts: Maintains a fixed-size FIFO table that receives rows through DAT methods.
Clamp and Max Lines control how many recent rows are retained.
Callbacks can run once for each row added to the FIFO table.
First Row preserves the header row while older data rows are discarded.
